title: Longest Balanced Run
statement:
A switch log `bits` contains only `0` (off) and `1` (on). A stretch of consecutive entries is **balanced** if it has the **same number of 0s and 1s**.

Return the **length of the longest balanced stretch**, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: Positions 2 to 7 (1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1) hold three 0s and three 1s.

hints.nudge: Count each 1 as +1 and each 0 as -1. What does a balanced stretch look like in the running total?
hints.pattern: Prefix sums with a hash map of the first index where each total was seen.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every stretch is O(n^2). Treat 1 as +1 and 0 as -1 and keep a running total. A stretch from j+1 to i is balanced exactly when the total after i equals the total after j. So remember the FIRST index where each total appeared (the empty prefix has total 0 at index -1). When the same total shows up again at i, the stretch since the first time has length i - first[total]. Keep the maximum. Never overwrite the first index, so stretches are as long as possible.
